grade.first_issue: In Subcase A, the statement that the left-hand side is odd “unless \(y=0\) or \(w=0\)” is false as written; it is odd in every case because \(5^y\) is odd and \(2^{z-x}5^w\) is even.
grade.summary: The factorization and valuation strategy correctly eliminates all cases and supports the unique solution \((0,0,0)\). The erroneous parity wording is immediately repairable and does not change the argument: the left-hand side is always odd, so \(x=3k+1\). The assumption \(x\le z\) should also be identified explicitly as a harmless relabeling of the two factors.
strengths: Correctly handles all boundary cases and reduces the positive case to \(c=2k\).
Correctly factors \(2024^{2k}-b^4\) and restricts both factors to primes \(2\) and \(5\).
The modulo \(3\) contradictions and final modulo \(11\) computation are valid.

errors.description: The parity assertion in Subcase A contains a false “unless” qualification, although the required corrected observation is immediate.
The proof says “assuming \(x\le z\)” without explicitly invoking symmetry to justify relabeling the factors.
